# Migration - [`--add-modules`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#standard-options-for-java)

There can be a situation when the Java runtime is not able to infer the module
graph and modules needs to be added manually. Consider the following two JAR
files as shown in the following table.

| JAR File     | JAR Type | Loaded As | Dependencies | Main Method |
| ------------ | -------- | --------- | ------------ | :---------: |
| `app.jar`    | Modular  | Automatic | `domain.jar` |   **YES**   |
| `domain.jar` | Modular  | Named     |              |     No      |

The `app.jar` is an automatic module and thus does not contain the
`module-info.class` (on purpose for demonstration purpose). It uses the
`demo.domain` module which needs to be added using the `--add-modules` option.

> ```
> --add-modules module[,module...]
> ```
> Specifies the root modules to resolve in addition to the initial module. The
> `module` also can be `ALL-DEFAULT`, `ALL-SYSTEM`, and `ALL-MODULE-PATH`.
([reference](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/java.html#standard-options-for-java))

This should be considered as a **temporary solution** until the module is
properly updated to include the `module-info.java` file with the necessary
requires.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   └── domain.jar

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

   All modules available on the module path

3. Describe the JAR files

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   ```

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   No module descriptor found. Derived automatic module.

   demo.app automatic
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application fails to launch because the domain module is not loaded. As
   the application module is an automatic module, the Java module system cannot
   resolve its dependencies, preventing the domain module from being loaded.

   ```
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: demo/domain/Quote
       at demo.app/demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:8)
   Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: demo.domain.Quote
       at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
       at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
       ... 1 more
   ```

   Add the `demo.domain` module to the list of root modules using the
   `--add-modules` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --module-path './target/libs' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   This time the application works and prints the following.

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   ```

   (*Optional*) Load the `app.jar` as an unnamed module (using the
   `--class-path` instead).

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/app.jar' \
     --module-path './target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   This will produce the same quote.

   ```
   Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning. by Albert Einstein
   ```
